items.headline: ICE and Trade[XYZ] plan US perpetual futures market on Hyperliquid
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, and crypto startup Trade[XYZ] announced plans for a US market offering round-the-clock perpetual futures across crypto, equities, commodities and currencies. The launch is subject to regulatory approval.
items.sourceTitle: NYSE owner takes Trade[XYZ] stake as it plans US Hyperliquid futures

items.headline: Public firms' share of blockchain revenue has doubled since 2022
items.summary: A 1kx report says publicly traded companies now capture a larger portion of blockchain revenue, linked to institutional adoption and real-world use cases.
items.sourceTitle: Public companies double share of blockchain revenue since 2022: Report

items.headline: Polymarket halts trading after reported drain of user funds
items.summary: The prediction market platform paused trading after saying a third-party provider had been compromised. Reports also claim user funds were drained.
items.sourceTitle: Polymarket suspended trading amid reports of user funds being drained

items.headline: HTX and KuCoin Pull Back From Key International Markets
items.summary: Exchanges HTX and KuCoin have announced withdrawals from international markets, with HTX leaving the UK after a settlement with regulators and KuCoin halting services in Russia and Belarus. The moves add to a wider trend of exchanges exiting markets amid regulatory enforcement and sanctions compliance.
items.sourceTitle: HTX Exits UK After FCA Settlement as KuCoin Abandons Russia and Belarus

items.headline: Unidentified large holder withdraws $290 million from DeFi nightly, Aave rates rise
items.summary: Bitquery tracked a temporary liquidity squeeze as funds left DeFi near midnight. A milder snapshot appeared on October 29, when borrowing rates were lower.
items.sourceTitle: Mystery whale pulls $290 million from DeFi every midnight as Aave borrowing rates triple

items.headline: Polymarket halts trading following breach at outside vendor
items.summary: Polymarket has paused trading after one of its third-party providers was compromised, and users reported their accounts were drained.
items.sourceTitle: Polymarket suspends trading after third-party breach leads to user losses

items.headline: Walmart Bars Its Shares From OKX-ICE Tokenized Trading Venue
items.summary: Walmart, Eli Lilly, Cigna, Carnival and Arcos Dorados have objected to their shares being traded on the planned OKX-ICE tokenized stock venue. The objections bring the total to 38 companies.
items.sourceTitle: Walmart Blocks Its Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Trading Venue

items.headline: Russia Names NAUFOR as First Crypto Exchange Self-Regulator
items.summary: The Bank of Russia has approved NAUFOR as the country's first self-regulatory organization for crypto exchanges and digital depositories.
items.sourceTitle: Russia Approves Securities Group to Oversee Crypto Exchanges

items.headline: French Senate passes bill on automatic crypto tax data exchange
items.summary: The French Senate has approved legislation that would allow tax authorities across countries to automatically share information about crypto-asset taxation. The bill still needs to clear the rest of the legislative process.
items.sourceTitle: French Senate adopts bill for automatic sharing of crypto tax data

items.headline: Polymarket launches ultra-short crypto prediction contracts on its US platform
items.summary: Polymarket has introduced new Up/Down crypto contracts for its U.S. platform. The move comes as the CFTC revisits whether the prediction market complies with terms it agreed to when it returned to the U.S. in 2022.
items.sourceTitle: Polymarket brings ultra-short crypto prediction markets to U.S. platform

items.headline: ICE to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to US markets
items.summary: NYSE parent ICE plans to partner with and invest in Trade[XYZ] to launch regulated perpetual futures built on Hyperliquid for US customers. The move comes as HYPE's token price rose sharply.
items.sourceTitle: HYPE surges 15% as NYSE parent ICE moves to bring Hyperliquid perps to US

items.headline: US Treasury sanctions crypto launderers tied to North Korean IT workers
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury has sanctioned ten individuals and one entity, including two Russian crypto intermediaries, over laundering proceeds from North Korean fake IT worker schemes that help fund its weapons programs.
items.sourceTitle: U.S. Treasury Sanctions Crypto Launderers Behind North Korea’s Fake Workers

items.headline: KuCoin halts services in Russia and Belarus amid EU sanctions
items.summary: KuCoin has stopped serving customers in Russia and Belarus, effective immediately across all products. Affected users will get individual deadlines to close positions and withdraw funds, the exchange said, citing legal and regulatory requirements.
items.sourceTitle: KuCoin Exits Russia and Belarus as EU Crypto Sanctions Tighten

items.headline: Uniswap Labs opens TJAR fee conversion tool to outside apps
items.summary: Uniswap Labs has made its Token Jar fee conversion system available to other applications via a new tool called TJAR. The first app mentioned is Robinhood.
items.sourceTitle: Uniswap Labs opens fee conversion tool TJAR to apps, starting with Robinhood

items.headline: A chart bitcoin traders should watch closely right now
items.summary: An analyst highlights a market at an inflection point that could influence inflation trends and risk assets, including bitcoin and tech stocks.
items.sourceTitle: The chart bitcoin traders should be paying attention to

items.headline: Chainlink Falls 21% in October Despite Steady Exchange Outflows
items.summary: LINK has seen tokens leave Binance for 18 straight days, yet its price is down about 21% this month. A large earlier deposit may account for part of the outflow streak.
items.sourceTitle: Chainlink Loses 21% in October Even as Tokens Keep Leaving Exchanges

items.headline: UNI slips below $7 as new wallet addresses hit six-year high
items.summary: Uniswap's UNI token has fallen back under $7 after briefly recovering above that level this week. Meanwhile, new UNI addresses reached a six-year high, though the excerpt does not say what this signals for price.
items.sourceTitle: UNI’s 6-Year Wallet Spike May Not Mean What It Looks Like

items.headline: AI-discovered flaws can crash bitcoin nodes on Windows and Macs
items.summary: Three vulnerabilities found by a language-model scan have been made public. They are the first disclosed under Bitcoin Core's new rules for bugs that are easy to find.
items.sourceTitle: AI found a way to crash bitcoin nodes on Windows and Macs. It's now public

items.headline: Ripple Nears $900M Revenue Run Rate as XRP Expands
items.summary: Ripple is reportedly approaching a projected $900 million annualized product revenue run rate, driven by expanding institutional custody and payment channels for XRP. The company's strategy spans payments, trading, treasury management and digital asset infrastructure.
items.sourceTitle: Ripple Roars Toward $900M Milestone as XRP Gains Wall Street Access

items.headline: 33 major firms block tokenized stocks; Apple and Tesla silent
items.summary: JPMorgan, Coca-Cola and 31 other companies reportedly used a new SEC veto to stop tokenized shares trading on OKX and ICE's venue. Apple and Tesla have not commented.
items.sourceTitle: 33 Wall Street Giants Block Tokenized Stocks, But Apple and Tesla Stay Silent

items.headline: Analysts Debate Whether Bitcoin Could Fall Like Silver
items.summary: Benjamin Cowen warns Bitcoin could follow silver after a fake-out, while Charles Edwards expects limited downside. The excerpt gives no further detail on either view.
items.sourceTitle: Could Bitcoin Price Crash Like Silver? Warning Signs Are Showing

items.headline: Ibis Emerges From Stealth With $250M FalconX Credit Facility
items.summary: Onchain credit platform Ibis has launched publicly, backed by a $250 million credit facility from FalconX. The company also closed a pre-seed funding round.
items.sourceTitle: $250M FalconX Facility Powers Ibis Push Into Onchain Credit

items.headline: Ethena Pay's 11x leverage loop raises concerns over hidden losses
items.summary: The story examines how borrowing costs and funded exits affect the returns left for users of the Ethena Pay vault. It notes that the vault's actual leverage and controls have not been verified.
items.sourceTitle: Ethena Pay’s 11x leverage loop promises high yield, but risks hidden losses

items.headline: Datavault AI Reports Losing Access to Its Bitcoin Holdings
items.summary: Datavault AI says it has been unable to withdraw its Bitcoin from Biconomy since June. The company also plans to restate four financial reports linked to a Scilex deal.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin Treasury Datavault AI Says It Can’t Access Its BTC, Stock Tanks

items.headline: Aviva Investors adds tokenized share class to liquidity fund
items.summary: Aviva Investors is adding a tokenized share class to its Sterling Liquidity Fund on the XRP Ledger, backed by a £50 million commitment. The fund is described as being worth £22 billion.
items.sourceTitle: Aviva’s £50m tokenized fund: What changes for investors

items.headline: Strategy shareholders back daily dividends on four preferred stocks
items.summary: Strategy, the largest Bitcoin treasury company, has won shareholder approval for daily dividend payments on its preferred securities. Payments on STRC are set to start in November, with three other preferred stocks following in January 2027.
items.sourceTitle: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks

items.headline: GRVT Burns 1.1 Million Tokens Ahead of Grvt 2.0 Launch
items.summary: Grvt, a self-custodial trading platform on its own zero-knowledge chain, said its Foundation completed a first token buyback, burning 1.1 million GRVT tokens on the open market. The buyback is roughly 1% of circulating supply and comes before four planned product milestones leading to Grvt 2.0.
items.sourceTitle: GRVT Burns 1.1 Million Tokens as Countdown to Grvt 2.0 Begins

items.headline: Exchange and DeFi Breaches Drive Most 2026 Crypto Hack Losses
items.summary: Lightning.news data cited by Bitcoin Magazine puts net 2026 crypto hack losses near $2.35 billion after freezes and returns. September alone accounted for about $768 million, led by a Bitget wallet drain and a Liquid Network bug.
items.sourceTitle: Centralized Exchange and DeFi Losses Dominate 2026 Crypto Hacks Despite Hardware Wallet Failures

items.headline: DTCC moves toward blockchain for securities with major banks
items.summary: The DTCC's tokenization service has gone live on the Canton Network and the Besu private chain. Twenty firms, including JPMorgan, Citi and Morgan Stanley, have signed up to use it.
items.sourceTitle: Wall Street backbone DTCC brings $30 trillion securities closer to blockchain with major banks

items.headline: Former Goldman and BlackRock Staff Raise $4M for Onchain Loans
items.summary: Birch Hill, founded by alumni of Goldman Sachs and BlackRock, closed a $4 million seed round led by Multicoin Capital. The startup aims to bring U.S. loans onto blockchain rails through a regulated approach.
items.sourceTitle: Goldman, BlackRock Alumni Raise $4 Million to Put Farm and Apartment Loans Onchain

items.headline: Spiral Says Bitcoin Payments Face Demand Problem, Not Technology
items.summary: Spiral, the Bitcoin team linked to Block, argues that Bitcoin payments are held back by weak demand rather than technical limits. The group points to Stripe and Visa turning to stablecoins instead.
items.sourceTitle: The Real Threat to Bitcoin Payments Isn’t Tech, Jack Dorsey’s Team Says

items.headline: Bitcoin apps may overpay fees due to two library bugs
items.summary: Wallet and other apps that import PSBTs can miscalculate miner fees and miss excessive-fee warnings when they depend on a vulnerable library's accounting. The issue is tied to two bugs in that library.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin apps risk massive fee drain, and 2 library bugs are blamed

items.headline: Bithumb breached via employee system amid South Korean cyberattacks
items.summary: Crypto exchange Bithumb was hacked through an internal employee system, which it says is separate from its trading platform. The exchange is still determining whether customer information was exposed.
items.sourceTitle: Bithumb hacked through employee system as South Korean financial firms face cyberattacks

items.headline: CFTC reportedly revives Polymarket probe amid soldier insider-betting case
items.summary: The US derivatives regulator is reportedly reopening an investigation into Polymarket. A soldier's insider-betting case involving a VPN is being used to test the agency's authority over swaps.
items.sourceTitle: The Soldier, VPN and $400K Test To CFTC's Reach as Polymarket Probe Returns

items.headline: Why Crypto Firm Due Diligence Goes Beyond Blockchain Analytics
items.summary: The piece argues that compliance teams assessing virtual asset service providers must look beyond blockchain analytics to understand who they are dealing with. It uses banking and payments scenarios to illustrate the point.
items.sourceTitle: Why VASP Due Diligence Goes Beyond Blockchain Analytics

items.headline: Why crypto depositors may lose everything in bankruptcy
items.summary: Offshore corporate structures used by some crypto platforms can leave retail depositors exposed to losses when those platforms fail. Roshan Dharia says customers may unknowingly give up legal ownership of their assets, making them unsecured creditors in bankruptcy.
items.sourceTitle: Why Crypto Depositors Could Lose Everything in Bankruptcy

items.headline: Bitcoin approaches $81,000 before Fed decision; ZEC rises 8%
items.summary: Bitcoin is nearing the $81,000 level ahead of a Federal Reserve decision, while ZEC gained about 8%. Other major tokens outperformed bitcoin as tech stocks also rose.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin nears $81,000 ahead of Fed decision as ZEC jumps 8%

items.headline: Bitcoin Miner Luxor Secures $16 Million to Grow AI Business
items.summary: Bitcoin mining technology firm Luxor raised $16 million in a funding round led by CMT Digital. The money will support its push into artificial intelligence infrastructure.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin Mining Firm Luxor Raises $16 Million to Accelerate AI Expansion

items.headline: Ripple and C2FO Plan Faster Invoice Settlement on XRP Ledger
items.summary: Ripple and C2FO are bringing invoice financing and settlement to the XRP Ledger, using Ripple's dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD. The aim is to cut bank transfer delays that can leave suppliers waiting days for early payments.
items.sourceTitle: Ripple and C2FO Tap XRP Ledger to Turn Payment Delays Into Seconds

items.headline: VanEck debuts multi-asset ETF with stocks, bonds and Bitcoin
items.summary: VanEck has launched a new Wealth Builder ETF that mixes stocks, bonds and Bitcoin exposure. The fund targets a 2% Bitcoin allocation, within a permitted range of 1% to 5%, via a spot Bitcoin ETP.
items.sourceTitle: VanEck launches diversified ETF combining stocks, bonds and Bitcoin exposure

items.headline: Robinhood Chain raises $26 million as crypto revenue climbs in Q3
items.summary: Robinhood's blockchain helped lift the company's crypto revenue during the third quarter. Separately, its prediction markets generated $173 million in the same period.
items.sourceTitle: Robinhood Chain brings in $26 million as crypto revenue rises 20% in Q3

items.headline: Robinhood Earnings Fall Short as Crypto Revenue Climbs
items.summary: Robinhood reported record revenue of $1.42 billion but earnings per share of $0.51 came in below expectations. Crypto revenue edged higher, while prediction market activity on sports and elections grew to $173 million.
items.sourceTitle: Robinhood Misses Q3 Earnings as Crypto Revenue Rises and Prediction Market Bets Grow

items.headline: Robinhood's Crypto Revenue Falls 55% in Q3 Despite Record Total
items.summary: Robinhood posted record overall quarterly revenue of $1.42 billion, driven by options and prediction markets, while crypto transaction revenue fell 55% year over year. The company also expanded its blockchain and digital asset businesses.
items.sourceTitle: Robinhood Crypto Revenue Plunges 55% in Q3 Despite Record $1.42B Overall Revenue

items.headline: Bessent frames crypto as a tool to sustain dollar dominance
items.summary: Speaking at Ripple's conference, the U.S. Treasury Secretary said SEC and CFTC action could fill a gap left by the stalled Clarity Act. He also addressed curbing crypto debanking.
items.sourceTitle: Treasury's Bessent sees crypto as America's next tool for keeping the U.S. dollar on top

items.headline: Stacks founder says quantum concerns may be curbing Bitcoin growth
items.summary: Muneeb Ali, speaking on Cointelegraph's Chain Reaction podcast, cautioned that doubts about Bitcoin's resilience to quantum computing could discourage institutional investors.
items.sourceTitle: Quantum fears already limiting Bitcoin’s growth, Stacks founder says

items.headline: Robinhood's crypto revenue drops 55% yearly yet beats analyst expectations
items.summary: Robinhood's crypto revenue declined 55% compared with a year earlier but still came in above Wall Street forecasts. Crypto trading volume fell 38% from the prior-year level, while its broader blockchain business reportedly gained traction.
items.sourceTitle: Robinhood's crypto revenue fell 55% from last year, but topped Street forecasts

items.headline: Robinhood Adopts Ripple's Stablecoin, Treasury Software and Lending
items.summary: Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin now runs on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp, with a planned rollout to the Robinhood app later this year. The companies are also expanding their work together in treasury and institutional trading.
items.sourceTitle: Robinhood Taps Ripple's Stablecoin, Treasury Software and Trading Loans

items.headline: Robinhood Shares Drop After Q3 Miss Despite Crypto Revenue Beat
items.summary: Robinhood stock fell after hours after its third-quarter earnings missed estimates, even though crypto revenue came in above analyst forecasts.
items.sourceTitle: Robinhood Stock Falls After Q3 Earnings Miss: Why Didn't the Crypto Beat Help?

items.headline: Ripple wins final US approval for national trust bank
items.summary: Ripple said the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted final approval for its national trust bank, which will manage RLUSD reserves. The decision came despite objections from traditional banking groups.
items.sourceTitle: Ripple gets final US trust bank approval. What does XRP gain?

items.headline: Bitcoin Holds Near $80K Amid Election and Fed Concerns
items.summary: Bitcoin is trading in a narrow range around $80,000 after repeatedly struggling at $80,500. Traders are cautious ahead of the US midterm elections and macro uncertainty weighs on sentiment.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin Price Stalls at $80K as US Midterm Election, Fed Jitters Mount

items.headline: Gamdom Hit With $15M Bitcoin Ransom Demand After Alleged Breach
items.summary: Crypto casino Gamdom has received a $15 million bitcoin ransom demand from the extortion group Whitearmor, which claims to hold records for 15.4 million accounts. Gamdom disputes the size of the alleged database, and the claim follows a separate hot-wallet attack that cost the platform over $3 million.
items.sourceTitle: Crypto Casino Gamdom Faces $15M Bitcoin Ransom After Multimillion-Dollar Hack

items.headline: Ripple gains final OCC approval for trust bank backing RLUSD
items.summary: Ripple has received final approval from the OCC for a federally supervised trust bank. The bank will manage reserves for the RLUSD stablecoin and provide custody services, as banking groups challenge crypto charters in court.
items.sourceTitle: Ripple Wins Final OCC Approval for Trust Bank Behind $2.6B RLUSD Stablecoin

items.headline: Zcash co-founder urges halting grants program funding
items.summary: Sean Bowe argues the Zcash Community Grants program already has sufficient funds to keep supporting projects. He proposes redirecting its share of newly issued ZEC into a network reserve instead.
items.sourceTitle: Zcash co-founder calls to stop funding ‘over $125M’ grants program

items.headline: Crypto wallets shift focus away from simply adding more tokens
items.summary: Wallet providers once competed by listing the hottest coins first, but a flood of short-lived meme coins has changed that approach. The piece examines why token count alone is no longer a winning strategy.
items.sourceTitle: Why Having More Tokens Is No Longer Enough for Crypto Wallets

items.headline: Strategy Shareholders Vote on Daily Dividends for STRC Preferred Stock
items.summary: Strategy shareholders will vote Wednesday on whether STRC becomes what the company describes as the first security paying dividends every calendar day. The special meeting starts at 10:00 a.m. ET on October 28.
items.sourceTitle: Saylor Has 33% of the Vote and Needs 17% More for STRC Daily Dividends

items.headline: Ripple receives final approval for U.S. national trust bank
items.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has approved Ripple National Trust Bank, according to an announcement by Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse on X. The excerpt is brief and gives no further details.
items.sourceTitle: Ripple gets a final go-ahead to launch its own U.S. national trust bank

items.headline: Ripple Extends RLUSD Stablecoin Into Corporate Cash Management
items.summary: Ripple Treasury is offering returns on qualifying holdings of its dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD, aimed at idle corporate operating cash. The expansion also includes around-the-clock operation and AI tools for cash and payments management.
items.sourceTitle: Ripple Takes RLUSD Into Corporate Cash Management With 24/7 Returns

items.headline: Ripple receives final US approval for national trust bank charter
items.summary: Ripple has gained final US approval for a national trust bank. The approval allows the firm to manage reserves backing its RLUSD stablecoin and offer digital asset custody.
items.sourceTitle: Ripple wins final US approval for national trust bank

items.headline: Three payment rules shape Aave's native Bitcoin market, only WBTC settles them
items.summary: A proposed direct route from Babylon could bypass pool funding for Aave's native Bitcoin market. Fees, borrower surplus and WBTC-denominated debt still carry separate payment requirements.
items.sourceTitle: 3 payment rules control Aave’s native Bitcoin market, but only WBTC settles them

items.headline: Moody's Flags Crypto Crash Among Likeliest Economic Risks
items.summary: Moody's risk matrix ranks a crypto crash as one of the most likely economic risks. Concerns about AI, Iran and bonds have also grown ahead of the Fed's rate decision.
items.sourceTitle: Moody’s Warns Crypto Crash Is Among the Most Likely Economic Risks

items.headline: US banking regulator urges community banks to issue payment stablecoins
items.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency is encouraging community banks to become issuers of payment stablecoins. The move follows the regulator finalizing its rules under the GENIUS Act, a stablecoin law set to take effect in January.
items.sourceTitle: US OCC calls on community banks to become payment stablecoin issuers

items.headline: Injective debuts onchain futures tied to Nvidia GPU rental prices
items.summary: Injective has launched a futures market that tracks rental costs for five Nvidia GPUs. The product offers leveraged trading and could serve as a hedge against swings in AI computing expenses.
items.sourceTitle: Injective launches onchain futures market tracking Nvidia GPU rental costs

items.headline: Vultisig wallet update fixes critical private key leak risk
items.summary: An August update addressed a flaw that could let an already-compromised signer recover a private key through many malicious signing messages. The bug involved an application ignoring a critical stop condition.
items.sourceTitle: August updates block critical private key leak in crypto wallet Vultisig

items.headline: CoinDCX Admits $16 Million Loss After Earlier Dismissal
items.summary: Indian exchange CoinDCX says 15.99 million USDT was drained from wallets it had retired following a prior hack, pushing total losses near $60 million. The firm says it will cover the loss itself.
items.sourceTitle: India’s CoinDCX Confirms $16 Million Loss Days After CEO Called It a ‘False Alarm’

items.headline: South Korea may again delay crypto income tax to 2029
items.summary: South Korean lawmakers are reportedly considering postponing a crypto income tax policy first set in 2020. The reported reason is concerns about receiving data from US officials.
items.sourceTitle: South Korea lawmakers mull pushing crypto tax implementation to 2029

items.headline: Card Fraud Scheme Tied to Bitcoin Ends in Prison Sentence
items.summary: A Rochester man received a prison sentence after running a fraud scheme that pushed unauthorized card payments through bank accounts to fund bitcoin purchases. He was named as Timothy Wadsworth.
items.sourceTitle: From Stripe to Bitcoin: Card Fraud Case Ends in Prison Sentence

items.headline: Hong Kong picks Nasdaq-listed Solana firm as strategic enterprise
items.summary: A Nasdaq-listed company focused on Solana plans to set up validator operations in Hong Kong. The excerpt does not give further details about the designation.
items.sourceTitle: Hong Kong names Nasdaq-listed Solana Company a strategic enterprise

items.headline: Bitcoin slips under $80,000 as analyst's bearish roadmap gains attention
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $80,000, and analyst Benjamin Cowen has reportedly marked two of nine bearish steps as complete. Upcoming Federal Reserve and PCE data are also being watched as possible catalysts.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin Falls Below $80,000: Is Benjamin Cowen's Bearish Q4 Roadmap Playing Out?

items.headline: Bank of Israel Turns Down Netanyahu's Crypto Sanctions Workaround Idea
items.summary: The Bank of Israel said the country should focus on preventing possible international sanctions from affecting its economy rather than seeking crypto-based ways around them. Netanyahu had said other alternatives to crypto could achieve the same goal.
items.sourceTitle: Bank of Israel Rejects Netanyahu’s Crypto Sanction-Evasion Plan

items.headline: Bitcoin and gold rank as worst major assets of 2026
items.summary: Charlie Bilello's data shows Bitcoin and gold as the weakest major assets of 2026, a first in his records. The excerpt links the performance to oil prices and Federal Reserve policy.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin and Gold Hit a Historic First in 2026. The Two “Safe Havens” Are Now the Worst Assets

items.headline: Bitcoin's Seven-Day Hashrate Climbs Back to 1 ZH/s
items.summary: Bitcoin's network hashrate has returned to the 1 zettahash per second level, meaning miners are again performing over one sextillion calculations each second. The excerpt notes this comes as miners continue securing the network and competing for newly minted bitcoin.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin’s 7-Day Hashrate Returns to 1 ZH/s After Nearly 8 Months

items.headline: US Bitcoin ETFs Post $138M Outflows; Zcash Keeps Inflows
items.summary: U.S. bitcoin ETFs recorded about $137.94 million in net outflows on Friday, closing a week marked by sharp swings between inflows and selling. Ether saw modest inflows, while Zcash and NEAR also drew fresh capital.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $138M as Zcash Extends 3-Day Inflow Streak

items.headline: Fed Week Sets Up Key Moves for Stocks, Bitcoin and DXY
items.summary: A busy week of central bank decisions and PCE inflation data comes alongside an $11 billion Bitcoin options expiry. The excerpt does not detail specific outcomes or expectations.
items.sourceTitle: Fed Week Puts Stocks, Bitcoin, and DXY on Collision Course Before $11 Billion Expiry

items.headline: Bitcoin Challenge Site Offers $2,000 to Hackers, Unclaimed So Far
items.summary: A website offering $2,000 in bitcoin to anyone who can steal it remains unclaimed. An independent review suggests the challenge may be practically impossible to crack.
items.sourceTitle: Website Dares Hackers to Steal Bitcoin as the Clock Keeps Ticking

items.headline: Six More Firms Object to Trading Their Shares as Tokens
items.summary: Twenty-two companies have now objected to their shares being traded on a planned tokenized stock venue run by OKX-ICE. Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit and others recently joined the opposition.
items.sourceTitle: Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit Among 6 More Companies Objecting to Tokenized Stocks

items.headline: Keystone customers claim breach exposed data that was supposed to be deleted
items.summary: Customers say a breach revealed information the hardware wallet maker had pledged to delete. Keystone has said it generally erases customer data 180 days after orders, though some X users have questioned that claim.
items.sourceTitle: Keystone customers say breach exposed data the hardware wallet maker promised to delete

items.headline: ECB official links digital euro to EU monetary sovereignty
items.summary: Piero Cipollone, an ECB official, says the bloc plans real-transaction tests in 2027 and a possible digital euro rollout as early as 2029. Both timelines depend on legislation expected this year.
items.sourceTitle: ECB official sees digital euro as key to protecting EU ‘sovereignty’

items.headline: Hyperliquid Leads Perps Market as HYPE Token Slides
items.summary: The HYPE token has fallen about 22% from its September peak near $98, even as the decentralized platform holds roughly $7.7 billion in open interest. Analysts note its market share in real-world asset trading is shrinking.
items.sourceTitle: Hyperliquid Still Rules the Perps Market, but HYPE Bulls Face Trouble

items.headline: Netanyahu suggests blockchain could help Israel evade possible sanctions
items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said ahead of elections that the country could turn to blockchain and crypto to get around potential international sanctions. The idea drew criticism from opponents and the central bank governor.
items.sourceTitle: Netanyahu floats use of blockchain as solution to potential financial sanctions

items.headline: Bitcoin hashrate recovers to 1 ZH/s despite miners shifting toward AI
items.summary: Large public Bitcoin miners are reallocating capacity toward artificial intelligence, yet the network's hashrate is still rising. The seven-day average has reportedly returned to around the 1 ZH/s level.
items.sourceTitle: Miner Weekly: Bitcoin Hashrate Shrugs off the AI Unplug, Regaining 1 ZH/s Level
